newsitem.title: USA: Nebraska legislators approve mail order sales tax.
newsitem.headline: Nebraska legislators approve mail order sales tax.

text.p: Nebraska lawmakers have approved a bill requiring direct marketers outside its borders to turn over customer information that will allow the state to collect sales taxes from residents who use the services, the legal counsel to the legislature's revenue committee said Thursday.
Nebraska loses up to $20 million in sales tax revenues annually, but lawmakers have not estimated how much money could be recouped through the bill approved Wednesday, George Kilpatrick said.
Practically speaking, the bill would most likely force direct marketers to sign voluntary collection agreements under which they would remit sales taxes to the state, Kilpatrick said.

Nebraska Gov. Ben Nelson vetoed a similar bill in 1995 and is in the process of reviewing the current version, spokesman Karl Bieber said. He had serious reservations about the past proposal and does not see much of an improvement, he said.
Nelson has until Tuesday to sign or veto the measure or it automatically becomes law, Bieber said.
